newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - Aug 5.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Kia creditors on Monday said they would extend emergency loans to core units of the troubled conglomerate but only under conditions the group has repeated rejected. The creditors said they would extend the bail-out period by two months.

- "Grandma Hun", a self-confessed Korean sexual slave for the imperial Japanese military during World War two who spent most of her life in Combodia, realised a life-long dream on Monday by returning to Korea.
- Heavy rains hit South Korea for two consecutive days by Monday, causing property losses and death in landslides and floods caused by the torrential rain.
- Four-nations talks, including the two Koreas, the U.S. and China, will take place in New York on Tuesday, to set a date and venue for peace talks.

- The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said in a report released on Monday that facilities investment by the nation's 200 largest companies in the second half of this year would decrease 7 percent to 19,247 billion won.

- The United States is expected to drastically lower the price of E-767 Airborne Warning & Control System (AWACS) in an offer to be made to Korea in September and has verbally notified Seoul officials of the new offer, a U.S. government official stationed in Seoul said.
